105.title: PSYC 105 Wireframe Basics
105.scope: Module 2 neuroanatomy plus clearly marked supporting visual vocabulary; no Modules 11+ content.

direct: PSYC 105 Study Guide, Module 2, page 1: identify the four cerebral lobes and their broad functions.
sourceNotes.supporting: Supporting visual vocabulary requested for this study tool; not an explicitly listed objective in the supplied course study guide. Forebrain directions and section planes follow standard anatomical conventions.
sourceNotes.conventions: Directions describe the human forebrain, not the spinal cord. Surface views and section planes are different concepts. Yellow pathways are schematic connections, not individual measured tracts; their endpoints determine the tract class. Highlighted shapes are teaching representations, not diagnostic images.

questions.prompt: Which brain region is highlighted in the wireframe?
questions.explanation: The highlighted region occupies the front of the cerebral hemisphere, ahead of the central sulcus. Look for the front of the hemisphere. The frontal lobe lies anterior to the central sulcus.
choiceExplanations: The highlighted region occupies the front of the cerebral hemisphere, ahead of the central sulcus. Look for the front of the hemisphere. The frontal lobe lies anterior to the central sulcus.
The parietal lobe lies behind the central sulcus and above the temporal lobe. That upper cortical territory is not the highlighted structure.
The temporal lobe lies along the lower side of the cerebrum, below the lateral sulcus. The highlight identifies a different region.
The occipital lobe occupies the back of the cerebral cortex. It is different from the highlighted region and is not the cerebellum beneath it.

questions.sourceNote: Shared visual foundation: PSYC 108 Midterm 1 Study Guide, page 1, and Review, page 10. White-matter tract classes are supporting material, not separately listed PSYC 105 Module 2 objectives.
questions.prompt: Which white-matter tract class matches the endpoints of the yellow connection?
questions.explanation: The yellow path joins two cortical areas within the same hemisphere. That endpoint pattern defines an association tract.
choiceExplanations: A ventricle is a space containing cerebrospinal fluid. The yellow line represents a connection between neural regions, not a fluid-filled cavity.
The yellow path joins two cortical areas within the same hemisphere. That endpoint pattern defines an association tract.
Commissural tracts connect the two cerebral hemispheres. The yellow path does not show that cortex-to-cortex connection across the midline.
Projection tracts link cortex with subcortical or spinal levels. A connection between two cortical areas does not have that endpoint pattern.

flashcards.sourceNote: PSYC 108 Midterm 1 Review, page 6: dorsal/superior, ventral/inferior, rostral/anterior, and caudal/posterior.
flashcards.question: For this human forebrain, which term names the direction shown by the arrow?
flashcards.answer: Rostral. Rostral points toward the front, or nose end, of the human forebrain; here it matches anterior. Follow the arrow relative to the brain, not relative to your screen.

flashcards.sourceNote: PSYC 108 Midterm 1 Review, page 6: dorsal/superior, ventral/inferior, rostral/anterior, and caudal/posterior.
flashcards.question: For this human forebrain, which term names the direction shown by the arrow?
flashcards.answer: Caudal. Caudal points toward the rear of the human forebrain; in this diagram it matches posterior. Follow the arrow relative to the brain, not relative to your screen.

flashcards.sourceNote: PSYC 108 Midterm 1 Review, page 6: dorsal/superior, ventral/inferior, rostral/anterior, and caudal/posterior.
flashcards.question: For this human forebrain, which term names the direction shown by the arrow?
flashcards.answer: Superior. Superior points toward the top of the human forebrain; in this diagram it matches dorsal. Follow the arrow relative to the brain, not relative to your screen.

flashcards.question: For this human forebrain, which term names the direction shown by the arrow?
flashcards.answer: Inferior. Inferior points toward the bottom of the human forebrain; in this diagram it matches ventral. Follow the arrow relative to the brain, not relative to your screen.

flashcards.sourceNote: PSYC 108 Midterm 1 Review, page 6: dorsal/superior, ventral/inferior, rostral/anterior, and caudal/posterior.
flashcards.question: For this human forebrain, which term names the direction shown by the arrow?
flashcards.answer: Anterior. Anterior points toward the front, or nose end, of the human forebrain; here it matches rostral. Follow the arrow relative to the brain, not relative to your screen.

flashcards.sourceNote: PSYC 108 Midterm 1 Review, page 6: dorsal/superior, ventral/inferior, rostral/anterior, and caudal/posterior.
flashcards.question: For this human forebrain, which term names the direction shown by the arrow?
flashcards.answer: Posterior. Posterior points toward the back of the human forebrain; in this diagram it matches caudal. Follow the arrow relative to the brain, not relative to your screen.

flashcards.question: For this human forebrain, which term names the direction shown by the arrow?
flashcards.answer: Medial. Medial points toward the midline that separates the left and right cerebral hemispheres. Follow the arrow relative to the brain, not relative to your screen.

flashcards.sourceNote: Supporting visual vocabulary requested for this study tool; not an explicitly listed objective in the supplied course study guide. Forebrain directions and section planes follow standard anatomical conventions.
flashcards.question: For this human forebrain, which term names the direction shown by the arrow?
flashcards.answer: Lateral. Lateral points away from the midline, toward the outer side of a cerebral hemisphere. Follow the arrow relative to the brain, not relative to your screen.

flashcards.sourceNote: Supporting visual vocabulary requested for this study tool; not an explicitly listed objective in the supplied course study guide. Forebrain directions and section planes follow standard anatomical conventions.
flashcards.question: Which surface view of the brain is shown?
flashcards.answer: Lateral view. You are looking at the outer side of a cerebral hemisphere. This is a lateral surface view, not a cut through the brain.

flashcards.sourceNote: Supporting visual vocabulary requested for this study tool; not an explicitly listed objective in the supplied course study guide. Forebrain directions and section planes follow standard anatomical conventions.
flashcards.question: Which surface view of the brain is shown?
flashcards.answer: Medial view. You are looking at the inner surface of a cerebral hemisphere, facing the midline. The other hemisphere is removed to expose that surface.

flashcards.sourceNote: Supporting visual vocabulary requested for this study tool; not an explicitly listed objective in the supplied course study guide. Forebrain directions and section planes follow standard anatomical conventions.
flashcards.question: Which surface view of the brain is shown?
flashcards.answer: Superior view. You are looking down onto the brain from above. This is a superior, or dorsal, surface view of the human forebrain.

flashcards.sourceNote: Supporting visual vocabulary requested for this study tool; not an explicitly listed objective in the supplied course study guide. Forebrain directions and section planes follow standard anatomical conventions.
flashcards.question: Which surface view of the brain is shown?
flashcards.answer: Inferior view. You are looking up at the underside of the brain from below. This is an inferior, or ventral, surface view of the human forebrain.

flashcards.sourceNote: Supporting visual vocabulary requested for this study tool; not an explicitly listed objective in the supplied course study guide. Forebrain directions and section planes follow standard anatomical conventions.
flashcards.question: Which anatomical section plane is highlighted through the wireframe?
flashcards.answer: Sagittal plane. The highlighted plane separates left and right portions of the brain. At the exact midline, it is specifically a midsagittal plane.

flashcards.sourceNote: Supporting visual vocabulary requested for this study tool; not an explicitly listed objective in the supplied course study guide. Forebrain directions and section planes follow standard anatomical conventions.
flashcards.question: Which anatomical section plane is highlighted through the wireframe?
flashcards.answer: Coronal plane. The highlighted plane separates front and back portions of the brain. Coronal is also called frontal; it is a section plane, not a cerebral lobe.

flashcards.sourceNote: Supporting visual vocabulary requested for this study tool; not an explicitly listed objective in the supplied course study guide. Forebrain directions and section planes follow standard anatomical conventions.
flashcards.question: Which anatomical section plane is highlighted through the wireframe?
flashcards.answer: Horizontal plane. The highlighted plane separates upper and lower portions of the brain. For these forebrain images, horizontal is also called axial.

flashcards.sourceNote: PSYC 108 Midterm 1 Study Guide, page 1, and Midterm 1 Review, page 10: association, commissural, and projection fibers.
flashcards.question: Which white-matter tract class matches the endpoints of the yellow connection?
flashcards.answer: Association tract. The yellow path joins two cortical areas within the same hemisphere. That endpoint pattern defines an association tract.

flashcards.sourceNote: PSYC 108 Midterm 1 Study Guide, page 1, and Midterm 1 Review, page 10: association, commissural, and projection fibers.
flashcards.question: Which white-matter tract class matches the endpoints of the yellow connection?
flashcards.answer: Commissural tract. The yellow path links cortex in one hemisphere with cortex in the other hemisphere. That left-right connection defines a commissural tract.

flashcards.sourceNote: PSYC 108 Midterm 1 Study Guide, page 1, and Midterm 1 Review, page 10: association, commissural, and projection fibers.
flashcards.question: Which white-matter tract class matches the endpoints of the yellow connection?
flashcards.answer: Projection tract. The yellow path links the cortex with a lower central nervous system level. Cortex-to-subcortical or spinal connections are projection pathways.
